name: Tofu Bao
steps: Mix flour, yeast, baking powder, sugar and salt. Add the warm dough water and 10 ml oil; knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and let rise for 60 minutes or until doubled.
While the dough rises, press tofu between clean towels for 20 minutes, then cut into 16 thick rectangles. Cut cucumber and carrot into thin matchsticks and keep chilled.
Coat the dry tofu lightly with cornflour. Heat the 20 ml oil in a nonstick pan and fry tofu in a single layer for 3 minutes per broad side, until crisp and golden; remove to a plate.

Lower the heat and cook garlic and ginger in the same pan for 30 seconds. Add soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar and glaze water; simmer for 2 minutes. Return tofu and turn gently for 1 minute until the reduced glaze clings to it.

Deflate and divide dough into 8 equal balls. Roll each into an oval about 12 cm long and 5 mm thick. Brush the inside surfaces with the reserved 5 ml oil and fold loosely in half. Set each bun on a small piece of baking parchment, cover and proof for 30 minutes until puffy.

Arrange buns with space to expand in a steamer above simmering water, without touching the water. Steam covered for 12 minutes; turn off the heat and wait 3 minutes before opening the lid gradually. Steam in batches if needed.
Gently open the warm buns. Fill each with 2 tofu pieces, cucumber and carrot strips, sharing the remaining glaze across the buns. Serve immediately.
tips: Make the filling during the dough rises, then warm it before filling. Keep glaze thick so it does not soak the buns.
passiveTime: Allow 90 minutes for dough rising and proofing.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
